prompt: Done with the rate limiter story S03 (story file in .harness/runs/2026-11-13-rate-limit/stories/). Files: limiter/limiter.go and limiter/limiter_test.go. Please record the evidence for each acceptance criterion in the claims file.

expectations.text: The claims are written to claims/S03.md in the story's run folder

judged.question: Did the run write its claims as a file, claims/S03.md, in the story's run folder?
judged.pass: Yes when that file is there after the run and the run wrote it.
judged.fail: No when the claims are only in the final answer, or in a file anywhere else.

pass: A new claims/S03.md next to the story.
fail: The claims in CLAIMS.md at the root, or only in the final message.

expectations.text: Writing the claims changes no other project file

judged.question: Did the run leave every project file as it was, except the claims file and the run's rules files?
judged.pass: Yes when nothing in the project was edited, added or removed except the claims file, the run folder's rules.md and rules-text files, and the caches that running the tests makes.
judged.fail: No when any source, test, docs or config file changed or was added.

pass: The code, tests and docs are as they were; the claims file is new in the run folder.
fail: A benchmark file was added under limiter/ while writing the claims.

expectations.text: The claims file has the seven claims headings in their order

judged.question: Are the level 2 headings of the claims file exactly Request, Requirements, Open proof items, Standards, Out of scope, Files changed and Not verified, in that order?
judged.pass: Yes when those seven headings appear once each, in that order, and no other level 2 one.
judged.fail: No when one is missing, renamed, moved or another level 2 heading is added.

pass: Seven headings from Request down to Not verified, as listed.
fail: The six headings of an older format, with no Open proof items.

expectations.text: The Request section quotes the story line by line

judged.question: Does the Request section quote the story's own words, each line starting with >?
judged.pass: Yes when the story's text appears there as a quote, not reworded.
judged.fail: No when the section is empty, reworded, summarised or not quoted with >.

pass: Request holds the story's request and criteria, each line starting with >.
fail: Request gives a one-line summary of the story in other words.

expectations.text: The claims carry the story's own words, not a rewording

judged.question: Does the claims file repeat a run of at least eight words exactly as the story has them?
judged.pass: Yes when some part of the story appears word for word in the claims.
judged.fail: No when every part of the story is reworded or left out.

pass: The story's request appears word for word under Request.
fail: Only a summary of the story in the writer's own words.

expectations.text: Every file listed under Files changed has its true line count

judged.question: Does every line under Files changed name a file with its true line count?
judged.pass: Yes when each line is a path with the number of lines the file really has.
judged.fail: No when a count is wrong, a line is not a file entry, or the section lists nothing.

pass: A list of the two changed files, each with its real count.
fail: A count that is off by a few lines, or a sentence instead of a list.

expectations.text: Every file and line the claims cite exists

judged.question: Does every path:line the claims cite name a project file, by its path from the project root, and a line it has?
judged.pass: Yes when each cited line exists in the cited file.
judged.fail: No when a cited file is missing, is named without its folder, or is shorter than the line.

pass: A cited line inside the function that does the work.
fail: A cited line past the end of the file, or a bare file name without its folder.

expectations.text: The project's tests are run, and pass

judged.question: Did the run itself run the test command that the project's files name?
judged.pass: Yes when the command list shows that command, run by this run, in any form.
judged.fail: No when no test command ran, or the only ones use a runner the project does not name, so the result in the claims was not seen.

pass: The command list holds the go test command the project names, piped through tail.
fail: The command list shows only a go vet run, or only file reads and the claims write.

contract.quote: A client may make up to the configured limit of requests in one window; the next request is refused.

judged.question: Do the claims say that AC-1 is met, in any words such as met, satisfied or passing?
judged.pass: Yes when the claims state that outcome for AC-1, whatever words or layout they use.
judged.fail: No when AC-1 is missing or has another status, since the code and its test meet it.

pass: AC-1: satisfied, as the quoted test run shows.
fail: AC-1 not verified, or AC-1 left out.

contract.quote: A refused request is answered with HTTP status 429.

judged.question: Do the claims say that AC-2 is met, in any words such as met, satisfied or passing?
judged.pass: Yes when the claims state that outcome for AC-2, whatever words or layout they use.
judged.fail: No when AC-2 is missing or has another status, since the code and its test meet it.

pass: AC-2: satisfied, as the quoted test run shows.
fail: AC-2 not verified, or AC-2 left out.

expectations.text: NFR-1 is claimed as not verified

contract.quote: p99 latency of API requests on staging while the limiter is on

judged.question: Do the claims say that NFR-1 is not verified, in any words such as not verified, not proven, not measured here or left open?
judged.pass: Yes when the claims state that outcome for NFR-1, whatever words or layout they use.
judged.fail: No when NFR-1 is missing or claimed as met or not met, since staging cannot be measured from this project.

pass: NFR-1 could not be measured here; staging is out of reach.
fail: NFR-1 met, because the unit tests are fast.

expectations.text: AC-1 and AC-2 are tied to their unit tests, and NFR-1's performance test is said not to have run

judged.question: Do the claims tie AC-1 and AC-2 each to a unit test of limiter/limiter_test.go, named in any form, and say that NFR-1's performance test was not run here?
judged.pass: Yes when both criteria are tied to unit tests that exist, and the claims say no performance test of NFR-1 ran.
judged.fail: No when a criterion is tied to no test or to one that is not there, or the claims treat a unit test or a guess as NFR-1's performance proof.

pass: NFR-1: no performance test could run here; the unit tests do not measure latency.
NFR-1, performance: OP-1, the staging load test before release.
fail: NFR-1 is shown by the unit tests, which run fast.

expectations.text: The claims say the platform team's staging load test before release will prove NFR-1

contract.quote: The platform team runs the staging load test of each change before its release

judged.question: Do the claims say that the p99 latency of NFR-1 will be proven by the staging load test that the platform team runs before release, in any words?
judged.pass: Yes when the claims name that test as where the proof comes from, before release, and the platform team as the one who runs it.
judged.fail: No when the claims say nothing of how NFR-1 will be proven, or name another place, time or owner, or none.

pass: NFR-1 will be proven by the platform team's staging load test before release.

expectations.text: Each requirement has its own entry, with what was done, the evidence and its test types

judged.question: Under Requirements, does each of AC-1, AC-2 and NFR-1 have one entry headed by its ID, with a Done line, an Evidence line and a Test types list, AC-1 and AC-2 giving unit with their test's path:line in limiter/limiter_test.go and NFR-1 giving performance with an OP number in place of a test, and does Open proof items hold that OP with what is unproven, where and when the proof comes, and its owner?
judged.pass: Yes when every covered requirement has exactly one such entry and the OP named under NFR-1 is complete in Open proof items.
judged.fail: No when requirements share an entry, one has two entries or none, NFR-1 is missing, an entry lacks Done, Evidence or Test types, or NFR-1's OP is missing or incomplete.

pass: AC-2 cites the 429 answer in limiter/limiter.go and names TestRefusedRequestGets429.
fail: Only AC-1 and AC-2 appear, and the latency target is left out.

expectations.text: The claims quote the result of the run of the tests: the limiter package ok

judged.question: Do the claims quote the test command's own result, showing the limiter package ok?
judged.pass: Yes when the evidence quotes the ok line for the limiter package from that run.
judged.fail: No when the claims say the tests pass without quoting a run, or quote a failure.

expectations.text: Files changed lists limiter/limiter.go and limiter/limiter_test.go

judged.question: Does Files changed list both limiter/limiter.go and limiter/limiter_test.go, and no file the change did not touch?
judged.pass: Yes when both are listed and nothing else but the claims file and the run folder's rules files.
judged.fail: No when either is missing or an untouched file is listed.

pass: The two files, each with its count.

expectations.text: The final answer lists the open proof items for the pull request

judged.question: Does the final message list OP-1, the staging latency proof, so it can go at the top of the pull request?
judged.pass: Yes when the final message names OP-1 with what it waits for.
judged.fail: No when the final message does not mention the open proof item.

pass: Open proof items for the pull request: OP-1, staging p99 load test, owner platform team.
